Crochet Diamond Shawl Pattern + Tutorial

Sharing is caring!

  • Email
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by

Instaread

The Crochet Diamond Shawl is made with Red Heart Super Saver Bitty Stripes yarn. It's really long, at 75" long by 20" wide. I've always wondered about edging that wasn't flat, and this pattern opened my eyes to possibilities for this type of concept.

Each strip is made on its own, then attached as you go. The request for this tutorial came in on our YouTube channel, and I took a look. I hadn't seen this pattern on Yarnspirations before, as there are literally about eleven thousand patterns to sift through.

Colour Control Tip

See how the stripes look as you crochet them. They aren't sewn together; they're made with a join-as-you-go concept. If you want more control over your coloring with solid colors, consider Red Heart Super Saver instead of the watercolor look of Red Heart Super Saver Bitty Stripes.

GET PATTERN

Mikey's Notes

I found this pattern easy to do, and it has a stitch multiple of 8 chains + 4. This means you can adjust the size to whatever you want.

The forward pass across the chain requires counting the chains, but as soon as you turn around, the slip-stitch spots and the center points of the circles are obvious. The return pass on the underside of the chain will go much faster.
